Indo-Surinamese, known locally as Hindustanis, are the descendants of indentured labourers brought from British India to Suriname from 1873 to 1916. The first ship, the Lalla Rookh, landed on 5 June 1873.

After the end of slavery, planters needed new workers. Under a treaty with Britain, some 34,000 Indians came on five-year contracts, most from what is now Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Many stayed and became rice farmers and traders, keeping Hindu and Muslim faiths and the Sarnami language.

They became the largest single group in Suriname, about a quarter of its people. The same system brought Indians to Guyana and to Trinidad, as part of the Indian indenture that followed the end of slavery across the Caribbean.
